issues.description: Title/CHANGELOG say 'not_publicly_shared' but PR description's check folder uses 'compute_image_publicly_shared' — contract name inconsistency
issues.detail: The metadata, file paths, and class name all consistently use 'compute_image_not_publicly_shared', but the PR description repeatedly references 'compute_image_publicly_shared'. The check name is the contract identifier callers and dashboards bind to; the discrepancy suggests the spec was not stated once and held. Pick one and propagate everywhere before merge.

issues.description: IAM-policy failure silently degrades to publicly_shared=False, weakening the check's postcondition
issues.detail: In _get_images, if getIamPolicy raises (e.g., permission denied, as test-image-3 simulates), the image is appended with publicly_shared=False and the check reports PASS. The supertype contract is 'PASS means we verified non-public sharing'; the implementation returns PASS when verification failed. Introduce an explicit 'unknown'/MANUAL state or surface an error finding so the postcondition is honest.

issues.description: Image ADT under-specifies its invariant: only stores a derived boolean, losing the binding context
issues.detail: The Image model carries publicly_shared: bool but drops which role(s) granted public access and the raw members list. Callers (remediation, audit logs) frequently need 'why' alongside 'whether'. Storing public_members or public_bindings on the ADT keeps the abstraction self-describing and avoids re-querying. Minor — the current contract is technically sound, but thin.

issues.description: Image ADT is missing resource self-link/URI invariant common to other compute ADTs
issues.detail: Disk, Instance, and other models in this service typically carry enough identity to be addressable (project + name is fine, but a uri/self_link would match the module's convention). Drawing the boundary consistently across compute ADTs reduces surprise for downstream consumers and reporting layers.

issues.description: Service-level test asserts on shared mutable state from sibling mocks, coupling unrelated tests
issues.detail: compute_service_test.py asserts images[2] (the permission-denied case) has publicly_shared=False. That conflates two possible reasons — truly not shared, or policy fetch failed. The test pins the current leaky behavior rather than the intended contract, making future correction (see P1) a test-breaking change.

review.summary: The new check is small and the ADT is mostly clean, but the contract is under-specified at two boundaries. First, the check name is inconsistent between the PR description and the shipped artifacts — the abstract identifier callers will bind to must be stated once. Second, and more substantively, the _get_images implementation silently coerces IAM-policy fetch failures into publicly_shared=False, which weakens the check's postcondition: a PASS no longer means 'verified not public', it means 'either verified or we could not tell'. The Image ADT itself is thin — it discards the bindings that justify its boolean — and the service test pins the leaky behavior. Decision: LEAKY-ABSTRACTION on the failure path; SPEC-MISSING on the name; otherwise ADT-SOUND.
